To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) scenario planning offers the opportunity to assess the value of a building in a more realistic way, by taking into account the uncertainty of future events; (b) scenario planning is not a new concept for architects and designers; however, it is a new approach in the life cycle assessment community and can be used to create a more holistic and realistic assessment; (c) scenario integrated life cycle assessment offers more nuanced outcomes, which are more relevant to decision-makers and designers, and (d)
scenario integrated life cycle assessment can be a powerful tool to understand and communicate the value of a design and its long-term financial feasibility.

scenario planning is a useful tool for assessing the value of a design decision in a life cycle perspective, that it is important to understand the value of a scenario, that the value of a building is not a static concept, that it is essential that the scenarios are developed by the stakeholders involved, that the scenarios need to be based on the same data set, and that the assessment should be repeated for every scenario.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of scenario planning into life cycle assessment.
the question how to better integrate scenario planning into life cycle assessment and how this can be used to improve the decision-making process.
the integration of scenario planning into life cycle assessments to better understand the value and financial feasibility of buildings.

scenario planning can be a powerful tool to raise awareness and create alternatives for the future.

the integration of scenario planning into the life cycle assessment of buildings is a valuable tool that can be used to assess the long-term value, financial feasibility, and sustainability of buildings.
the proposed methodological framework can be used as a tool for scenario integrated life cycle assessment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of scenario planning into life cycle assessment can help us better understand the long-term value and financial feasibility of buildings.

the integration of scenario planning into life cycle assessment can help us to better understand the value of a building, and that it can be a powerful tool to co-create more resilient and sustainable buildings.
scenario planning is a useful tool for raising awareness of the long-term value and financial feasibility of building designs and for identifying and evaluating design alternatives.

the integration of scenarios into life cycle assessments is a promising approach to better understand the value and financial feasibility of our building stock.
